question: How many of Japan's 47 prefectures will be at the influenza warning level (≥30 cases per sentinel institution) in the MHLW weekly report for the week ending October 25, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Only Okinawa is at or above 30 now (31.34 in wk41) and it is falling (37.07 to 31.34), so it likely drops below 30 by wk43. The nearest challengers are Kanagawa 21.6 (+17%/wk), Saitama 21.0 (+7%) and Chiba 19.6 (+4%); Tokyo is flat. National growth is modest (11.35 to 12.81). Each needs about +40% in two weeks to reach 30. Upside risk: school closures rose 1.8x and the wk42 holiday dip may be followed by a wk43 rebound; past seasons show growth of 50%/wk in the acceleration phase. Most likely outcome is 0 or 1, with a tail to several if the season accelerates. No human market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; I checked no other venues).

- wk41 prefectures: Okinawa 31.34 (only one >=30), Kanagawa 21.60, Saitama 20.99, Chiba 19.55, Hokkaido 16.21, Tokyo 15.88, Iwate 13.34, Yamaguchi 12.36.
- wk40 (Sep 28-Oct 4): national 11.35; Okinawa 37.07 (only one >=30), Saitama 19.66, Chiba 18.72, Kanagawa 18.51, Tokyo 15.87; 15-16 prefectures >=10.
- Week-over-week wk40 to wk41: Kanagawa +17%, Saitama +7%, Chiba +4%, Tokyo flat, Okinawa -15%. Okinawa down 2 consecutive weeks; Aichi down 3 weeks; Shizuoka and Okayama slightly down (Resemom).
- Weathernews: brief national dip in wk39, then rising again.
- School/class closures wk41: 1,703 facilities vs 937 the previous week (1.82x).
- wk42 (Oct 12-18) includes the Oct 12 Sports Day holiday, which may depress counts; MHLW wk42 release expected ~Oct 23; not found as of Oct 19.
- Reference: in the 2025/26 season, national went roughly 3.3 to 6.3 to 14.9 to 21.8 across late Oct to early Nov 2025 (rapid acceleration phase) [recall, not re-verified].
- To reach 30 by wk43, Kanagawa needs about +39% over 2 weeks, Saitama about +43%, Chiba about +53%.
- Resolves off MHLW per-prefecture per-sentinel figures for wk43 (Oct 19-25), published ~Oct 30; not off national average or prefectural alerts.
- Event window: single surveillance week Oct 19-25, 2026; as of Oct 19 it is just starting (0% elapsed).
- Status quo: 1 prefecture (Okinawa) currently >=30.

calls.reasoning: Two weeks remain from week 41 data (national 12.81, up from 11.35). Okinawa is declining 42.50->37.07->31.34 and should drop below 30 by week 43 if the trend holds. Hokkaido rose 9.2->16.2 (+76%) and is the most likely to cross 30. Iwate (13.3, +55%) is a long shot. Kanto (Kanagawa 21.6, Saitama 21.0, Chiba 19.6) has slowed to 0-17%/week and needs ~18%/week to reach 30. The week-42 Monday holiday (Oct 12) depresses counts. Searched Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers: no market found. Median 1, meaningful mass at 0, tail to 4+ if growth reaccelerates as it did in Nov 2025.

calls.reference_class: Japanese prefectures at 16-31 per sentinel during early-season weeks, and their status two weekly reports later; plus the 2025/26 season's week-by-week count of prefectures >=30 during the build-up phase

calls.reasoning: In week 41 only Okinawa (31.34) is at or above 30, and it has fallen about 15% a week for two weeks, so it most likely drops below 30 by week 43. The challengers are Kanagawa 21.6 (+17%/wk), Saitama 21.0, Chiba 19.6 and Hokkaido 16.2 (+76%/wk). Each needs roughly 18-40% weekly growth over two weeks to reach 30. National growth slowed to +13%, and the week-42 holiday blurs the trend. Base case is 0-1 prefectures, with a right tail if the season reaccelerates like Nov 2025.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on all checkable facts: week 40-41 prefecture values, Okinawa's decline, the week-42 holiday, and that no market exists. The only factual discrepancy, the count of prefectures above 10 in week 41, does not affect the outcome and was not settled. The real disputes are judgment calls. Which challenger is most likely to cross (Hokkaido's surge vs slowing Kanto): I treat both as live paths, which slightly fattens the 1-2 range and the tail. Whether Okinawa stays at 30 or above: likely not, given a steady ~15%/wk decline, but it keeps some mass at 1+. I carry Run 2's dispersion and broadly agree with all three runs' shapes, because the evidence supports a mode at 0-1 with a take-off tail. No market found (harness found none; no independent check this run).
